Subject: Data fencing decision request and SLA check — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Lena — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the deployment mode that meets Medisync's isolation expectations.

Recap from our call (short):
- Medisync is evaluating Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) vs Private VPC/on-prem for production inference.
- Primary concerns: strong data isolation guarantees, key management (BYOK), network egress controls, and predictable latency for realtime workflows.

Questions / clarifications we need from you to qualify next steps:
1) Isolation model: Do you require physical tenant separation (no noisy neighbor on shared hosts) or is strict network/logical separation inside a cloud VPC acceptable?
2) KMS: Will Medisync require customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for all model inputs/outputs and logs, or is vendor-managed with audit logs acceptable for POC?
3) Throughput/latency targets: What are your 99th pct latency SLO and peak concurrent requests (tokens/sec or reqs/min)?
4) Evidence list: please confirm which of the following artifacts you can share to speed qualification: architecture diagram, procurement timeline, current compliance requirements (SOC 2/HIPAA), and IP allowlist for egress.

What Redwood can offer (short):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with tenant-only nodes, SLA-backed throughput. Supports customer KMS, private peering, and single-tenant runtime.
- Private VPC: control plane in our hosted model but inference nodes deployed into your VPC (or on-prem connector). Strong network isolation, customer-controlled routing, and KMS integration.
- Hybrid: Dedicated pools inside a customer VPC for both capacity guarantees and network isolation — useful if you need tight performance and isolation simultaneously.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-options.pdf (high-level topologies) and data-isolation-checklist.pdf (artifact checklist).

Proposed next steps:
- Can we schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with your infra/security team? Ben (SE) and Marissa (Solutions) will join. We have availability: Wed 10/21 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 10/23 09:00–10:00 PT.
- If procurement needs be looped, share the contact and typical timelines (PO, SOW).

Thanks — want to make this as frictionless as possible. If you prefer, we can start with a Dedicated + VPC hybrid topology as a conservative default while we validate isolation artifacts.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medisync.io>

Subject: Re: Data fencing decision request and SLA check — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Thanks, Tessa — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: we are leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (customer VPC with vendor nodes) because of our networking team’s mandate to control egress and use internal KMS. That said, we also need guaranteed GPU capacity; we cannot tolerate bursty performance degrading our clinical inference SLA.

Quick answers to your list: 
1) Isolation model: logical isolation inside our VPC is acceptable provided we have no shared-host running our inference workloads and we can prove network egress control. Physical single-tenant would be ideal but is not a hard blocker if SLAs and telemetry are strong.
2) KMS: We require customer-managed KMS for model inputs and any persisted logs. HSM integration would be preferred.
3) Targets: 99th pct latency <= 120ms for single-turn requests at our normal load; peak is ~250 concurrent inference sessions (roughly 20 reqs/sec sustained, spikes up to 60 reqs/sec).
4) Evidence: we can share our compliance self-attestation and a network topology sketch. Procurement will need a clear pricing band and a sample SOW; I’ve CC’d procurement for timeline.

Procurement note: procurement@medisync.io — typical PO review takes 3–4 weeks; if we need exceptions for data residency or SLA we’ll surface that early.

Can do Wed 10/21 10:00 PT — please send calendar invite and agenda.

Cheers,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product — Model Integrations
Medisync Health
